transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hi. Yeah, um, well, honestly my supervisor is the one who told me I really needed to come see somebody. I work in production, down at the manufacturing plant, and I've been getting in a lot of trouble lately because I just... I keep leaving my station. 

It's like, I'm supposed to stay put right there at my machine on the line, but I just keep wandering off or popping up. Even during our morning shift meetings! We have these pre-shift meetings where everyone is just sitting on these awful metal folding chairs in the breakroom, and I just... I can't stay sitting. I'll just stand up right in the middle of it. And on the floor, it's way worse. My supervisor says it's becoming a really serious safety problem because of all the heavy machinery and the forklifts driving around the aisles. He says I just take off before I even think about it, which, I mean, he's not wrong. I don't even realize I'm doing it until I'm already halfway across the floor. My brain just says 'move' and my legs are already going before I remember I'm supposed to be glued to my spot. 

I mean, I get it, safety first and all that, and I'm not trying to cause trouble or get anyone hurt. It's just so hard to just stand in one little square taped off on the concrete for hours. But yeah, that's why I'm here. Because of the walking away thing. He basically said I'm a hazard right now and need to get it figured out.
Have you struggled with this kind of restlessness and needing to move around since you were a child in school, or is this something that started more recently?

Oh, wow, yeah, no, this is definitely not a new thing. Not at all. I mean, if you asked my mom, she'd probably tell you I came out of the womb trying to run a marathon. But yeah, school was... well, it was a disaster, honestly. Even way back in elementary school, I was always *that* kid. You know the one. The one who just could not, for the life of her, stay in her assigned seat. It was like those little plastic chairs they had were made of lava or something. I'd be up sharpening my pencil, or going to the trash can, or just wandering over to look at the class pet—we had a hamster named Barnaby in third grade, and I swear I spent more time at his cage than at my desk. 

And it wasn't just the moving around, either. I was constantly getting in trouble for talking. I'd just talk right over the teacher. Like, she'd be in the middle of explaining fractions or something, and a thought would pop into my head, and I just had to say it right then and there. I couldn't hold it in. It was like a sneeze, you know? You can't just hold in a sneeze. So I'd just blurt things out, completely interrupting the whole lesson. My backpack was basically just a delivery service for notes from the teacher to my parents. 'She's disruptive,' 'she won't stay seated,' 'she blurts out answers without raising her hand.' It was constant. So, yeah, this whole 'not being able to stay put and just doing things before I think' thing... it's been the story of my life since forever. It's just that now, instead of annoying a teacher, I'm apparently a hazard to myself and others around heavy machinery.
Outside of the physical restlessness, do you often have trouble keeping your focus on tasks that require sustained mental effort?

Oh my gosh, yes. It's not just the walking away thing, it's... well, it's anything that makes me sit still and actually use my brain for more than two seconds. 

Like, at work, they have us do these inventory logs sometimes, right? And lately, they've also been having me read over these CNC training pages because they were talking about cross-training me on the new machines before this whole wandering-off issue got so bad. Anyway, with both of those things, the logs and the training manuals, I really do try. I sit down and I tell myself, 'Okay, you are going to read this, you are going to do this right.' I start out really trying so hard to just focus. 

But honestly, after just a few minutes—maybe not even a few minutes, maybe like sixty seconds—the numbers on the inventory sheets or the words on the training pages just completely blur together. I'll be staring right at the paper, moving my eyes down the lines, but I'll get to the bottom of the page and realize I didn't take any of it in. Nothing. It's just completely blank up here. So then I have to keep going back to the top and starting over, over and over again, because none of it stuck the first time, or the second time. And it's so incredibly frustrating because it's just basic reading and counting, you know? It shouldn't be this massive, impossible chore, but I just can't keep my head locked onto the page no matter how hard I try to force myself. I just end up staring at a blurry wall of text.
